llm.summary: The package's code, CLI, and runtime instructions are consistent with a local full-conversation archival/search tool; requested capabilities (reading local session files, writing archives, running a local API, and optionally using git to back up) match the stated purpose, but there are privacy/operational cautions you should consider before enabling backups or running it with real data.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (full conversation memory, semantic search, archival) align with the provided code: session capture, archiving, search engines (TF-IDF/semantic), summaries, integrity checks, an API server, and auto-backup. Files and CLI subcommands directly implement the advertised features; no unrelated cloud credentials or external services are required by default.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts deliberately read local OpenClaw session files (~/.openclaw/sessions), write full conversation archives to a memory directory (default ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory), and can start a local HTTP API. This is coherent with the stated purpose but means the skill will collect and persist all conversation content (including assistant 'thought' content if present). The API binds to 127.0.0.1 (local) which reduces remote exposure, but running it still exposes data to any local processes and could be forwarded if the host is misconfigured.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (lowest install risk) but the bundle includes many Python scripts which will be executed locally when invoked. No remote downloads or package installs are performed by the skill itself. Because code is shipped in the skill, you must trust the contained scripts before running them, but there is no high-risk external installer or URL-based payload.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which matches most behavior. However, it legitimately invokes git (via subprocess) for automatic backup/push; if you configure a remote, pushing will use your system's git credentials/SSH keys—this could result in data leaving your machine if you set a remote. The code does not appear to require unrelated secrets or cloud tokens by default.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request forced/always-on privileges (always:false). It writes archives and may initialize a git repo inside the configured memory directory (its own data). It does not modify other skills' configs or system-wide settings beyond the memory directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill is coherent with its description: it captures OpenClaw session files and archives full conversations to disk and provides local search and a local HTTP API. Before installing/running: 

- Understand it will persist full conversations (user messages, assistant replies, and any captured 'thought' content) to your filesystem—this can contain sensitive data. 
- The capture looks for session files under ~/.openclaw/sessions and writes to ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory by default; you can and should override --memory-dir to a controlled location or sandbox. 
- Automatic backup uses git commit + push if you configure a remote; do not set a remote you don't fully control (or keep auto_backup disabled) to avoid accidental exfiltration. Git pushes will use whatever system SSH/credentials are available. 
- The bundled REST API listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 by default (local only) — avoid exposing that port to untrusted networks. 
- The repository contains many executable scripts; inspect the code (or run in an isolated environment/container) before giving it access to real conversations. 

If you want stronger assurance, ask for a focused review of the omitted files or run the test suite in an isolated environment; evidence of network calls to unexpected external endpoints or unconditional remote pushes would change the assessment to suspicious.
